Server/review.mjs uses a given --range verbatim, and its own refusal text suggests the two-dot form (michael/dev..worktree/<name>). A two-dot diff of a branch cut before newer michael/dev merges looks like it reverts them, so the reviewer may flag reverts that aren't there (seen on worktree/merge-list-module-tasks, 2026-10-23).
fix: In review.mjs, turn a two-dot range into three dots before diffing: const spec = range ? range.replace(/^([^.]+)\.\.(?!\.)/, "$1...") : ...; and change the refusal's example to michael/dev...worktree/<name>.

outcome.note: Server/review.mjs (053b06906): a two-dot --range becomes three dots before diffing; both refusal examples show michael/dev...worktree/<name>.

essence: Every worktree's dev server writes into tracked files.jsonl files (74 to 101 per worktree within minutes). The churn blocks `git merge` inside a worktree ("commit your changes or stash them") and blocks `git worktree remove`. On 2026-10-23 it hit worktree/qf-3 and worktree/smoke-ignored.
fix: A worktree's dev server should not write files.jsonl at all (they are listings the main tree keeps), or should write them to an ignored path. Fall back to `git update-index --skip-worktree` on them at worktree-up.

essence: Seven tests fail on michael/dev itself (the merge's near-tests run on 2026-10-23): fixer, TaskMove, landing-check, page_tools, global, item_tool, AskIndex-tasks. Merges no longer block on them, because they also fail on the base, so nobody is pushed to fix them.
fix: One cheap minion per failing test: get each one passing, or retire it with a reason. Then near-tests protects all 69.

essence: A freshly spawned minion's first prompt was blocked: "UserPromptSubmit hook callback timed out after 30000ms" (minion-qf3-work-tab, 2026-10-23 21:50 local). The minion went dormant having done nothing, and its parent got an empty "done:" report.
fix: Find which UserPromptSubmit hook took 30 s on a minion's first prompt; prompt-relay.mjs and the role reminder are candidates. Make it fail open: time-box it well under 30 s. Have Servex treat an empty first-turn report from a minion as a failed start (retry once), not as "done".

essence: append.mjs (Server/LogLine.mjs:31-36) stamps `at` on every line, including lines appended to a page.jsonl. On a page, Item.apply reads a top-level `at` as the old compat path key (core/Item/Item.js:119-124): the browser warns "no at target", and a nested `{content:{at,…}}` line is dropped. Seen 2026-10-23 on worktree/part-types (core/Page/parts/types/page.jsonl).
fix: When the target's basename is page.jsonl, LogLine stamps a top-level `ts` (as the item tool does) and never `at`. Alternative: refuse page.jsonl targets and point to the item tool.

outcome.note: Fixed in Server/LogLine.mjs (commit fae489967): a page.jsonl target gets a top-level ts, never at; other targets keep at. Documented in Server/doc/log-line.md.

essence: Fixed, FYI: `review.mjs <taskdir> <worktree> --range A..B` dropped the worktree argument (Server/review.mjs:703), so a page review screenshotted the main site, where an unmerged page is a 404, and the reviewer would judge a 404. Now a range keeps the worktree for the shots (michael/dev, the commit after 1f0eea774).
fix: Done on michael/dev: `else if (worktreeArg) worktreeDir = path.resolve(worktreeArg)`. Nothing more is needed unless the range should also read files from the worktree.

essence: A parent's reference line {"task":"<folder url>"} with no `as` makes a child with id "task" whenever the referenced log's line 1 has no id of its own (every task dir Servex opens on spawn). Two such references in one parent then collide: Session.apply_line / Task replay treat the second as "the same id moved home" and replace the first, so a child disappears and progress undercounts. Seen in core/Page/tasks/page-mastermind/task.jsonl lines 82 and 91 (qf3-work-tab/ and nav-rule/): its replay shows one child {"id":"task"}.
fix: core/Task/Task.js:354, in from_ref: also rename the default id, i.e. `if (kid.id === "tasks" || kid.id === "task" || as) kid.id = id;` (Task.replay's fallback id is "task" at line 337), so the child takes ref_id(ref), its folder name. Add a Task.test check: two refs to id-less logs in one parent stay two children.

outcome.note: core/Task/Task.js from_ref (814456cad): an id-less referenced log (replay fallback id "task") now takes its folder name, so two refs in one parent stay two children. Task.test check added; it fails without the fix, 61/61 pass with it.

essence: Since about 23:26 on 2026-10-23, every reviewer Servex spawns dies on its first prompt with "UserPromptSubmit hook callback timed out after 30000ms" ($0.001, one turn). That includes four for nav-links (reviewer-nav-links -1/-2/-3, transcripts 7a7945fb and 7ae5d755) and mastermind-page's reviewer-sessions-fit. It happened even after the 23:37 Servex restart, when /agents answered in 0.09 s. The .claude prompt-relay.mjs hook answers in 0.06 s by hand, so the stall is the SDK callback hook inside Servex (Agents.sdk_hooks: remind_hook or the spec's own hooks). review.mjs then records it as a [fix] "the reviewer wrote no review.md", so no page change can pass review now.
fix: Find which UserPromptSubmit callback a reviewer's session waits on: log the start and end of each callback in Agents.sdk_hooks for one spawn. Have review.mjs retry a start that cost nothing and say "reviewer failed to start (hook timeout)" instead of a fake finding. The merge-latest reviewer at 23:13 worked, so diff the hook code between then and 23:26.

essence: return_worktree refuses a pool slot whose only dirt is the worktree server's own files.jsonl churn: Pool.give_back (Servex/Pool.js:202) filters server logs out of own_dirt, but the `merge --ff-only` at :219 still fails ("Your local changes … would be overwritten") whenever michael/dev touched one of those files. The deputy hit this on qf-3 and qf-1 on 2026-10-24 00:13, and had to stop each slot's server, `checkout -- .` and fast-forward by hand.
fix: In give_back, just before the ff at Servex/Pool.js:219, stop the slot's server as salvage() does (this.kill(slot.server_pid, this.server_cmd(slot))), then restore the noise: `for (const d of await this.dirt(slot)) if (Pool.server_log(d.file)) this.restore(slot, d.file);`. Then ff and restart the server. Without the stop, the running server rewrites the files within a second (seen on qf-1). Test: a slot with one modified files.jsonl that dev also changed returns as ready.

essence: One session, three cost totals. For session-e00f55c9 on 2026-10-24 00:20, the report tab (AICost.report → item tool `summary`, landed 0fe5bc9b6) says $585.39. The desktop session page's stats bar (SessionWork.figures(root).rolled, worktree/qf-2 c7ec41dd7) says $885.14. The item tool answered about $915 at 20:46 on 10-23, so a total that should only grow went down. Law 6/7: one computation of a session's cost, which every surface reads.
fix: Decide which computation is right: compare Task.summary's own+children sum against SessionWork.figures for e00f55c9, and name what one counts that the other doesn't (likely the tab's own transcript cost or nested grandchildren). Make the other surface call the right one (SessionWork can read the item tool's summary, as AICost.report does). Add a test that the two pages print the same total for one session.

outcome.note: Fixed in f6fb247ed: Servex event loop stalled 19-86 s (sync process list, full-tree task walk, sync git in ready-to-merge) so the 30 s hook callbacks timed out. Now async/cached/child-process; review.mjs retries a zero-cost reviewer start 3 times and says so. No gap over 8 s since the 23:58 restart.
Fixed in 1e4d8f267 (Pool.give_back stops the slot server, restores server-log noise, fast-forwards, makes a fresh slot); test in pool-heal.test.mjs. Live after the next Servex restart.

Cause: Report tab = item tool summary (rebuilt logs, wake-up inflation removed); stats bar = sum of index.json snapshot usd (old inflated figure). Item tool is right. Fix sent to mastermind-deputy for worktree/qf-2: SessionStats takes the headline cost from AICost.ask(base) summary.cost.total; test that both pages print the same total. Per-row SessionWork figures stay snapshot-based for now.

essence: Servex/TaskLoop-steps.test.mjs fails on Windows at its last line: fs.rmSync(dir) → EPERM on the temp dir, every run, on michael/dev in the main tree too. It blocked a merge once (it passed on the base by luck, so merge.mjs read it as a regression). Adding loop.stop() before the rm plus maxRetries 5 did not fix it, so something else still holds the dir: the state_watch child, or a handle the Store keeps.
fix: Await the state_watch child's exit in TaskLoop.stop() (or give stop() a promise that resolves when the watcher process exits), call `await loop.stop()` before the rm, and then rm with maxRetries. If a Store keeps the file open, close it first. The tried patch is at $TEMP/deputy-scratch/taskloop-test-try.patch.

outcome.note: Fixed in b7526bf1b. Root cause was not the state_watch (the test never starts the loop): tick() runs follow_up_daily/handover_daily/undone_asks_daily, each execFile with cwd = the fixture dir, and a live child holds the dir on Windows. The fixture now has today's three daily outputs, so none start. 3 clean runs; no change to TaskLoop.js.

essence: Compaction can still run mid-turn and can hang forever. The CLI's own auto-compact fired six times mid-turn near 167k on ai-system-mastermind (2026-10-24, agent log "trigger":"auto"). Agent.compact() sets `compacting` with no timeout, so a /compact that never answers leaves the agent stuck. The owner wants compaction only between tasks, with a timeout.
fix: (1) Raise the CLI auto-compact threshold for Servex agents (CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE or the SDK option) above Servex's own between-turn line, so oversized()/nudge()/sleep_compact() always fire first. (2) A 10-minute timeout on `compacting`: clear it, log compact-timeout, return to idle. (3) Proposal, owner unsure: renew a singleton on a topic change or after 30 min idle above 100k, else resume (identity.md, "Long-lived roles").

A VS Code tab's MCP connection (.mcp.json, servex) carries no caller, so item/page tools with no `path` cannot find the tab's own session page; tabs must type their uuid path, which is the drift risk the owner raised (a typed path is now refused when it names no real session, page_tools.js resolve()).
fix: Give the tab's connection its id, e.g. "url": "http://servex.localhost/mcp?as=${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID}" if Claude Code expands that variable at connect time (test in one tab first); then own_page(ctx) resolves a uuid caller through session_file() like an agent id. Check what else keys on ctx.caller (Assistant.js `from`, by-stamps) before switching. Detail: core/Session/doc/identity.md "A typed id that drifts".

essence: Server/review.mjs reports "reviewer failed to run: fetch failed" for any review that takes over 5 minutes, even though the reviewer goes on and writes a good review.md. Node's built-in fetch gives up when no response headers arrive within 300 s, and `mcp("wait_for_agent", {timeout_s: 900}, 910000)` waits for a single response. Seen 2026-10-25 05:18Z on deputy/running-for: the reviewer started 05:13:44, the fetch failed at 05:18:49, and review.md was written at 05:19. Every full Opus review that runs long hits this, and the catch then overwrites review.md with the failure.
fix: In review.mjs, loop the wait: call wait_for_agent with timeout_s 240 (ms 250000) until the agent's state is no longer working, or 900 s have passed in total (both call sites, lines ~468 and ~819). Also stop the catch from overwriting a review.md the reviewer has written.

outcome.note: review.mjs: waitAgent() waits for the reviewer in 240 s slices (up to 900 s) at both call sites; the catch no longer overwrites a review.md the reviewer wrote. Committed on michael/dev.

text-check flags past-work.md over its 500-word limit on a routine task (mastermind-roles-and-settling: 581 words), but past-work.md is generated by `node Server/PastWork.mjs --task` and headed "do not hand-edit" — no agent can act on that flag. Also: the same text-check run flagged the task's `outcome` as a stale 63-word paragraph that had already been superseded by a later assign line a minute earlier (clarity's rewrite) — the check reads a point-in-time snapshot, so a flag can outlive its own fix.
fix: Either raise PastWork.mjs's own word budget to match the checker's limit, or have text-check skip files headed "do not hand-edit" (generated output). For the stale-flag case: have text-check re-run (or note its own timestamp) after a fix lands, so a flag doesn't read as open once the fix it was about is already in the log.

outcome.note: Server/text-check.mjs (d3c12608e): skips files headed do not hand-edit; checks the newest outcome after landing so a rewrite clears a stale flag.
